stemMd: The student wants to emphasise an inconvenience that a tide mill's design creates for the people who buy its flour. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The restored tide mill at Cleave Point, Devon, grinds flour for two hours on each falling tide.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Because a tide mill can grind only while its pond is emptying, its working hours move about fifty minutes later each day, so customers at Cleave Point have to consult a tide table to find out when the mill is open.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Water let out of a pond behind a dam turns a tide mill's wheel as the sea falls away outside.

options.label: D
options.textMd: A tide mill is a watermill driven by the rise and fall of the tide rather than by a river's current.

explanationMd:
Two conditions are packed into this goal, and both have to be met. The sentence must name an inconvenience, and the people inconvenienced must be *the customers*, not the miller and not the mill.

The long sentence ending with the tide table is the only option that mentions customers at all, and it reaches them through the design: the mill grinds only while the pond empties, that constraint drags the opening times almost an hour later each day, and the result is that buyers must check a tide table before setting out. Design, consequence, inconvenience, in that order.

Check by striking out any option that fails either condition. The definition and the description of the wheel both explain how the mill works with no consequence attached, and the Cleave Point sentence reports what that mill produces. None of the three names a person who is put out by anything, so none can emphasise an inconvenience.

distractorRationale.d: This is a definition. It distinguishes a tide mill from a river mill but attaches no consequence to that difference, so nobody is inconvenienced in it.
distractorRationale.a: This reports the mill's output and grinding time. Two hours of grinding per falling tide is a fact about the mill's operation, not a difficulty stated from the customer's side.
distractorRationale.c: This describes the mechanism that drives the wheel. It is the cause of the inconvenience rather than the inconvenience, and it never reaches the people who buy the flour.

accessibilityText: Using the six student notes about tide mills, choose the sentence that best emphasises an inconvenience the tide mill's design creates for its flour customers.

provenance.notes: Original item. The goal names a specific affected party, so the item turns on which sentence reaches the customers rather than on which is most informative.

review.author: digital-sat-wave4-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The goal asks for an inconvenience to flour buyers caused by the design. B links the design (grinds only while the pond empties) to the shifting hours and to customers needing a tide table. A is only implicitly inconvenient and does not mention buyers; C and D describe the mechanism with no inconvenience.

review.notes: Author's own solve and uniqueness check: Goal requires (i) an inconvenience and (ii) customers as the affected party. Only D mentions customers, and it links them to the design through the shifting hours. A and C are mechanism, B is output; none names anyone inconvenienced. Unique. Not published: awaiting a blind independent solve by a second party. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
